subject: Fwd: NimbusAI request — transient regional fleet bridging & sizing
messages:
From: Diane Park <diane@cloudops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: NimbusAI — request for transient regional fleet bridging during ramp

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from Nimbus procurement/ops. We have a major feature launch planned for Dec 20 and need predictable dedicated capacity while the product ramps. High-level ask: a temporary committed tranche that covers baseline production plus a burst buffer for first 8–10 weeks so we don’t hit cold-starts or throttles.

Target service characteristics:
- Production launch date: 2026-12-20
- Sustained inference load (estimated): 2.2M tokens/minute globally at T+6 weeks
- Latency SLO: 150–250ms p95
- Regions of interest: APAC (SG/HK), EU (Frankfurt), US (us-west)

Initial sizing request (Nimbus proposal):
- APAC: 60 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved with 20% burst headroom
- EU: 80 A100-equivalents reserved with 20% burst
- US: 120 A100-equivalents reserved with 15% burst

They attached their forecast and a short SLA appendix. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a phased commit (pilot in APAC first, then global), and what the lead time and costs look like?

Diane
NimbusAI — Head of CloudOps
(attachment: nimbus_forecast_q4.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Forwarding Nimbus's request — forecast attached.

Top asks from me:
- Quick sizing sanity-check and recommended node classes (A100-80 vs A40/Q4 variants) so we can give a cost-backed proposal.
- Feasibility of phased commit: APAC pilot (40 GPUs) + scale to full reserved counts over 6 weeks.
- Suggested contract structure: short-term committed tranche (3 months) + burst capacity (pay-as-you-go) or a blended price?

Priyom: please draft a deal structure and price bands. Lauren/Karthik: ops/product constraints, lead times, and any QoS caveats. Vivek: heads up — this looks like a near-term expansion for Q4 bookings.

Marissa

Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fw: NimbusAI — request for transient regional fleet bridging during ramp

Thanks — looked through their forecast and ran a quick back-of-envelope. Attaching the capacity spreadsheet (capacity_calc_q4.csv) with assumptions. Key points / proposal: 

Assumptions (short):
- "A100-equivalent" interpreted as A100-80GB perf baseline. Where cost matters we propose mixed node classes (q8 quantized on A40/Q4 class) but preserve latency SLO with pinning.
- 20% burst buffer = recommended initial safety margin for first 8 weeks.

Proposed committed sizing (rounded):
- US baseline: 120 A100-eq -> provision 150 A100-eq (includes 25% buffer for launch week volatility)
- EU baseline: 80 A100-eq -> provision 96 A100-eq (20% buffer)
- APAC baseline: 60 A100-eq -> provision 72 A100-eq (20% buffer)

Phasing recommendation:
- Phase 0 (pilot, Week -4 to -2): APAC pilot 40 GPUs (mix of A100 and quantized A40 nodes) to validate tails and KV caching behavior.
- Phase 1 (Week -2 to Launch): Scale APAC to full requested reserved amount, bring EU up to 50% of committed, US to 60%.
- Phase 2 (Launch + 8 weeks): move to full committed counts with transparent burst for sudden spikes (rate-limited).

Contract/price approach suggestion:
- 3-month committed tranche covering launch period with an optional auto-extension month-to-month.
- Price band: committed discounted rate for reserved units + premium for burst. Provide blended estimate in the attached csv.

Risks/ops items:
- Lead time: some node classes may require 10–14 days allocation lead time in APAC depending on inventory.
- Cold KV-cache effects during sudden ramp — recommend conservative cache warm-up plan and pre-warming script runs before Dec 20.
- Fallback: automatic routing to lower-cost quantized variants if latency and quality allow.

Attaching numbers. I can convert this into an offer sheet once we align on node classes and phasing.

Priyom
Senior Sales Manager — Enterprise
(attachment: capacity_calc_q4.csv)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fw: NimbusAI — request for transient regional fleet bridging during ramp

Thanks — operational notes from product/serving runtime: 

- Kernel/instance recommendation: For latency-sensitive paths we should prefer A100-80 for request-heavy endpoints. For batchable or background tasks, quantized A40/Q4 nodes are fine and will reduce cost by ~35% in our projections. 
- Autoscaling: we should avoid aggressive autoscaling during first 4 weeks post-launch; prefer manual scaling windows tied to traffic forecasts and MAP checkpoints.
- KV cache: ensure warmers run 12–24 hours pre-launch to reduce p95 spikes (see attached nimbus-MAP-v2.xlsx for suggested warm-up plan).
- Fallback policy: route non-critical requests to quantized variants automatically at 300ms p95 threshold; keep core critical flows on A100 pinned pools.

Lead times & constraints:
- APAC provisioning: 10 days typical for reserved capacity; expedited 72-hour fulfillment possible but with higher cost.
- EU provisioning: 7–10 days.
- US provisioning: 3–5 days.

Operational ask for Sales/Success: include a week-by-week mutual action plan (MAP) with clear warm-up tasks, traffic gating, and rollback criteria. I modeled a pilot in APAC (40 GPUs) and incremental increases in the spreadsheet.

Lauren
Principal Product Manager — Serving Runtime
(attachments referenced: nimbus-MAP-v2.xlsx)

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: NimbusAI — request for transient regional fleet bridging during ramp (proposal)

Diane / Nimbus team — thanks for the prompt details and forecast. Internal alignment complete; summarizing our proposed offer and next steps: 

Proposal summary:
- Committed tranche (3 months) covering launch + 8-week stabilization:
  - US: 150 A100-equivalent reserved (covers 120 baseline + 25% launch buffer)
  - EU: 96 A100-equivalent reserved (80 baseline + 20% buffer)
  - APAC: 72 A100-equivalent reserved (60 baseline + 20% buffer)
- Phasing: APAC pilot (40 GPUs) provisioned first for validation; full APAC + scaled EU/US by launch window.
- Pricing: blended committed rate for reserved units + metered burst billing. Formal offer sheet to follow (Priyom).
- Ops commitments: warm-up plan, pinned A100 pools for critical endpoints, quantized fallbacks for non-critical traffic, and weekly MAP checkpoints for first 8 weeks.

Attachments sent: nimbus-MAP-v2.xlsx (week-by-week MAP), capacity_calc_q4.csv (assumptions & pricing bands), req_sla_appendix.pdf (SLA notes).

Next steps:
1) Nimbus to confirm phasing preference (pilot-only APAC vs simultaneous multi-region pilot) by EOD Wed 11/25.
2) Priyom to send draft SOW/offer and DocuSign link (target: Thu 11/26).
3) Product/Infra to hold provisioning window: APAC pilot ready by 12/02 if doc signed and expedited inventory available.

Vivek — please note for Q4 capacity commitments. Finance/tpm: we will need the final price sheet and confirm whether expedited provisioning costs are acceptable.

Marissa
Director, Global Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
(attachments: nimbus-MAP-v2.xlsx, capacity_calc_q4.csv, req_sla_appendix.pdf)
